question.text: How many Japanese prefectures will report 10.00 or more influenza cases per sentinel site in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's Week 50 2026 report?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of prefectures with reported influenza cases per sentinel site of 10.00 or higher for week 50 (expected to be posted after December 13, 2026 for the week through that date) according to the MHLW's influenza [press releases](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou01/houdou_00025.html).
question.fine_print: If the resolution source does not publish the data, then [JIHS](https://id-info.jihs.go.jp/surveillance/idwr/article/influenza/article.html) may be used as a backup source.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-14: The MHLW press-release page lists weekly 2026/27 reports. The newest is dated Nov 13 (PDF 001768730), covering week 45. The prefecture-level PDFs would not render as text for me, so the prefecture counts below come from news reports that quote MHLW data. [MHLW](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou01/houdou_00025.html)
- The week 50 report (Dec 7-13) should be published around Fri 2026-12-18. The MHLW page warns that from 2025 week 15 the number of sentinel sites changed (acute respiratory infection surveillance began), so earlier years are not perfectly comparable. [MHLW trends page](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/houkokusuunosuii_00007.html)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-13 (week 45, Nov 2-8): national rate 11.00 per sentinel, up from 10.26 and the third straight weekly rise. **23 prefectures were at 10 or above.** Hokkaido was highest at 28.32, then Fukushima 21.08, Aomori 19.79, Iwate 19.74, Miyagi 18.45, Yamagata 18.36 and Ehime 17.71 (down from 27.89). Kagawa was lowest at 3.96. Rates rose in 33 prefectures and fell in 14. [CB News/Yahoo](https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/7063617937fe4b2b91ddc80b1716e2ca56d6684f), [Resemom](https://resemom.jp/article/2026/11/13/88307.html)
- Nothing settles the question yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: Nikkei Medical says reports are rising mainly in eastern Japan, with a possible decline in western Japan. [Nikkei Medical](https://medical.nikkeibp.co.jp/leaf/mem/pub/report/t253/202611/595250.html)
- 2026-11-13: Mainichi says the season started more than a month earlier than last year. [Mainichi](https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20261113/p2a/00m/0li/010000c)
- 2026-11-06 (week 44): national 10.26, back above the advisory level for the first time in three weeks. 19 prefectures were at 10 or above, led by Iwate 17.17, Aomori 16.63, Akita 15.72 and Yamagata 14.51. [CB News](https://www.cbnews.jp/news/entry/20261106175704), [Jiho](https://nk.jiho.jp/article/306529)
- 2026-10-30 (week 43): national 9.49, with 15 prefectures at 10 or above (Okinawa 17.39, Hyogo 15.02, Hokkaido 14.60, Saitama 13.65). [CB News](https://www.cbnews.jp/news/entry/20261030172706)
- 2026-10-23 (week 42): national 9.08, the first decline since the season began in week 34. Hokkaido plus 11 prefectures (12 in total) were at 10 or above. [Nikkei Medical](https://medical.nikkeibp.co.jp/leaf/mem/pub/report/t253/202610/594965.html)
- 2026-10-09: the national rate reached advisory level, with Okinawa at warning level. [nippon.com/Jiji](https://www.nippon.com/ja/news/yjj2026100900793/)
- Okinawa had an early peak of 42.50 in week 39 and fell to 12.95 by week 44. All 19 strains typed there this season were A(H1)pdm09. I could not find national subtype data. [Okinawa](https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/_res/projects/default_project/_page_/001/006/388/0842kenshutsu_graph.pdf)

## 4. Base rates
**Weekly count of prefectures at 10 or above this season:** 12 (week 42), 15 (week 43), 19 (week 44), 23 (week 45). Five weeks remain until week 50.

**Week 45 to week 50 in past seasons:**

| Season | Week 45 national | Week 45 prefectures ≥10 | Week 50 national | Week 50 prefectures ≥10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 21.82 | 29 (5 at 30 or above) | 36.96 (peak 51.12 in week 47) | not confirmed |
| 2024 | low, under 2 (from memory, not checked) | not found | 19.06 (up from 9.03) | 42 |
| 2023 | not found | not found | 29.94 | 46 (all but Okinawa) |
| 2022 | not found | not found | very low (from memory, not checked) | not found |

- 2025: the week 45 figures come from [JST Science Portal](https://scienceportal.jst.go.jp/newsflash/20251118_n01/). For week 50, the top five were Miyazaki 99.93, Fukuoka 75.39, Kagoshima 75.14, Kagawa 63.65 and Kumamoto 62.92, and Okinawa was 14.16. I could not confirm the week 50 count, but it was probably all or nearly all 47. [yakuzaishi-online](https://yakuzaishi-online.com/%E3%82%A4%E3%83%B3%E3%83%95%E3%83%AB%E3%82%A8%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B6%E3%81%AE%E7%99%BA%E7%94%9F%E7%8A%B6%E6%B3%81%EF%BC%88%E4%BB%A4%E5%92%8C7%E5%B9%B4%E7%AC%AC50%E9%80%B1%EF%BC%89%E3%80%90%E5%8E%9A/)
- 2024: Oita 37.22 and Fukuoka 35.40 were the two at 30 or above. [Tokyo IDSC](https://idsc.tmiph.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/assets/flu/2024/Vol27No13.pdf), [levelmap](https://kansen-levelmap.mhlw.go.jp/Hasseidoko/Levelmap/flu/2024_2025/2024_50/jmap.html)
- 2023: Okinawa had been the only prefecture below 10 for three straight weeks. [BCN](https://www.bcnretail.com/market/detail/20231225_388732.html)
- 2022: low season; I could not verify the week 50 value.
- **Pattern:** in the last three major seasons, week 50 fell in or near the main winter wave, and 42 to 47 prefectures were at 10 or above.
- **How 2026 compares:** at week 45 it is about half of 2025's level (11.00 vs 21.82) but far above 2024. Growth is slow, about 7% a week nationally. The wave is uneven: eastern and northern Japan are rising, while western Japan (Ehime, Hyogo, Okinawa, Fukuoka at 8.37) is falling after an early H1 wave. In 2024 the national rate doubled in a single week (9.03 to 19.06) and covered 42 prefectures by week 50. A season that peaked early in some regions may leave several western prefectures below 10.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on Japanese flu counts. None of the supplied market prices match this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly MHLW releases on about Nov 20, Nov 27, Dec 4, Dec 11 and Dec 18 (the week 50 report). These will show whether the eastern rise spreads west and whether western prefectures pick up again (for example a shift to H3 or B).
- Factors to watch: school-term transmission, falling temperatures in December, and vaccine uptake (Japan Times, 2026-10-09, reported a rush for flu shots). [Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/10/09/japan/science-health/japan-flu-cases-jump/)
- I did not look up a JMA seasonal outlook.

Sources: the links given inline above.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-13: The MHLW press-release page lists 10 weekly releases for the 2026/27 season, the newest dated Nov 13 (week 45). The data are in PDFs (e.g., [001768730.pdf](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001768730.pdf)) that my tools could not read, so the prefecture counts below come from news reports. [MHLW](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou01/houdou_00025.html)
- 2026-11-13: The latest data is week 45 (Nov 2-8). The national figure was 11.00 per sentinel site from 41,071 cases, and **23 prefectures (Hokkaido plus 22 prefectures) were at or above 10**. None exceeded 30: the highest was Hokkaido at 28.32. [Yahoo/CB News](https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/7063617937fe4b2b91ddc80b1716e2ca56d6684f), [ABEMA](https://times.abema.tv/articles/-/10288797)
- Week 50 covers Dec 7-13, 2026. Its release is expected around Dec 18.
- Backup source: JIHS posted its week 45 data on Nov 13. It has suspended its advisory/warning level map because the sentinel network changed in week 15 of 2025. [JIHS](https://id-info.jihs.go.jp/surveillance/idwr/article/influenza/article.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet, with five weekly reports still to come. The current value is 23, which sits inside the question's 4.5-40.5 range.
- 2026-11-13: Activity is concentrated in northern and eastern Japan. Fukushima was at 21.08, Aomori 19.79, Iwate 19.74, Miyagi 18.45, Yamagata 18.36 and Akita 16.56. Saitama was at 16.34 per its prefectural site. Western Japan, Kyushu and Okinawa are mostly falling: Ehime dropped from 27.89 to 17.71 and Hyogo from 12.07 to 10.47. Shizuoka (7.78) lifted its advisory, and Kagawa was lowest at 3.96. Cases rose from the previous week in 34 prefectures. [Resemom](https://resemom.jp/article/2026/11/13/88307.html), [Nikkei Medical](https://medical.nikkeibp.co.jp/leaf/mem/pub/report/t253/202611/595250.html), [Weathernews](https://weathernews.jp/news/202611/130221/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: Mainichi reports the season started more than a month earlier than last year. [Mainichi](https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20261113/p2a/00m/0li/010000c)
- 2026-11-13: Week 45 cases were about half the same week last season (84,183) and about eight times the week two seasons ago (5,266). About 1,325 schools and nurseries had flu-related closures, down from 2,451, but whole-school and whole-grade closures increased. [Weathernews](https://weathernews.jp/news/202611/130221/)
- 2026-11-06: Week 44 was 10.26 nationally (38,205 cases). I could not find how many prefectures were at or above 10 that week. [jiho](https://nk.jiho.jp/article/306529)
- 2026-10-30: Week 43 was 9.49, week 42 was 9.08 and week 41 was 12.81. The week 42 dip likely reflects the Oct 12 holiday. [jiho](https://nk.jiho.jp/article/306352)
- Early-to-mid Oct: The national figure first crossed the advisory level at 11.35, with Okinawa above the warning level. [Yahoo/TBS](https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/67ba4169996cc58afcba6e0c6612eb69972ce697)
- Unrelated: on 2026-11-13, avian flu was found in poultry in Chiba. This does not affect the human sentinel data. [nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/57366)

## 4. Base rates (prefectures at or above 10 per sentinel)
How each season moved from week 45 to week 50:
- **2025/26:** Week 44 was 14.90 nationally with 25 prefectures at or above 10. Week 45 was 21.82 with 29 prefectures. Week 50 was 36.96, after three weeks of decline from the peak, with 36 prefectures above 30 and essentially all 47 above 10 (the lowest seen were Akita at 13.28 and Okinawa at 14.16). [JST](https://scienceportal.jst.go.jp/newsflash/20251118_n01/), [jiho](https://nk.jiho.jp/index.php/article/204247), [Toyama](https://www.pref.toyama.jp/documents/50726/influ_202551w.pdf)
- **2024/25:** Week 45 was about 1 nationally. Week 49 was 9.03, and week 50 was 19.06 with **42 prefectures** at or above 10. [Tokyo IDSC](https://idsc.tmiph.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/assets/flu/2024/Vol27No13.pdf), [MHLW](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001359460.pdf)
- **2023/24:** This was an early season like this one. Week 44 was 21.13 and week 45 was 17.35 (I did not find that week's prefecture count). Week 50 was 29.94 with **46 prefectures** at or above 10 (every prefecture except Okinawa) and 23 above 30. [BCN](https://www.bcnretail.com/market/detail/20231225_388732.html), [BCN Nov](https://www.bcnretail.com/market/detail/20231117_379298.html)
- **2022/23:** Week 50 was 0.53 nationally. Very likely 0 prefectures were at or above 10, since the maximum in week 51 was 4.21. [jiho](https://nk.jiho.jp/article/177393), [MHLW](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001032733.pdf)

How this year compares:
- At 11.00 nationally, week 45 this year is below 2025 (21.82) and 2023 (17.35) at the same point, but far above 2024 and 2022.
- Growth has been slow, about 7.5% a week since week 42, unlike the sharp November climbs of 2023 and 2025.
- Week 50 has usually been near the seasonal peak. In seasons with a national figure of 19 or more in week 50, 42 to 47 prefectures were at or above 10.
- Caveat: since week 15 of 2025 the sentinel network is smaller (about 3,000 sites), so per-site values from before and after the change are not strictly comparable.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this question. None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly MHLW releases for weeks 46 to 49 are expected around Nov 20, Nov 27, Dec 4 and Dec 11. Week 50 is expected around Dec 18.
- Things to watch:
  - whether the spread in northern and eastern Japan (Hokkaido, Tohoku, Kanto) reaches western Japan, or western Japan keeps declining
  - the Nov 23 (Labor Thanksgiving) holiday, which can dampen the week 48 figure
  - school-closure trends
- I found no weather outlook or subtype/strain data relevant to these weeks.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 5 weeks. The week 50 report (Dec 7-13) is due around Dec 18, 2026.

(b) Week 45 (Nov 2-8, reported Nov 13, 2026): national rate 11.00 per sentinel, with 23 prefectures at 10.00 or above. The weekly counts have been 12, 15, 19 and 23 over weeks 42 to 45.

(c) If nothing changed, about 23 prefectures.

(d) If the trend continued:
- The count has been rising by about 4 a week. A straight extrapolation over five weeks gives about 40-43, but the count is capped at 47 and growth should slow as fewer prefectures remain below 10.
- National growth of about 7% a week compounds to roughly 15-16 by week 50. Because the wave is uneven across regions, that would mean roughly 28-35 prefectures at 10 or above.
- A December acceleration, which is typical, would push the count toward 40 or more.

(e) In past major seasons, week 50 fell in or near the main winter wave, with 42 to 47 prefectures at 10 or above. This season looks different in two ways:
- It started early with an H1 wave that is now fading in the west, in Okinawa, Ehime, Hyogo and Fukuoka.
- National growth is slow.

A five-week window can move the count by 15 to 20 prefectures in either direction.

(f) I found no markets on this. The question creator's range of 5-40 implies a central value in the 20s to 30s. Nikkei Medical notes rising activity in eastern Japan and a possible decline in western Japan.

(g) Low and high scenarios:
- **Low:** the early H1 wave has used up much of the susceptible population, eastern Japan peaks in late November, and the west keeps declining. That leaves around 8-15 prefectures above 10 at week 50.
- **High:** an H3 or B wave takes off in late November with school transmission and cold weather, as in 2024 when the national rate doubled in one week. That gives 44-47 prefectures.
